title: Adaptive kernel sampling & NVTX lifecycle tagging for per-kernel heatmaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce low-cost, high-fidelity per-kernel performance signals that can be correlated with scheduler decisions (prefill vs decode), attention path selection, and observed tail-latency. We need an adaptive sampling strategy plus deterministic NVTX lifecycle tags so traces and aggregated metrics can be stitched into the Console heatmaps and per-route dashboards.

Motivation: Current kernel metrics are noisy under variable load (oversampling under spikes, blind spots on tail events). We also lack lifecycle identifiers that let us tie a kernel invocation to the request-level scheduling decision (e.g., prefilling KV vs decode step) and to the attention implementation chosen at runtime (FlashAttention vs fallback). This ticket covers instrumentation design and a runtime PoC for production-configurable sampling + NVTX tagging and exporter labels.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can attach a short-lived lifecycle ID to NVTX ranges for all kernel launches (prefill, decode, attention, other compute) and include a kernel fingerprint label
Configurable sampling policy (probabilistic + rate limit) per route/model that controls which requests emit full NVTX spans vs coarse counters
Prometheus/OTLP exporter produces per-kernel aggregated metrics with tags: lifecycle_id (when sampled), kernel_fingerprint, attention_path, route, model_version
Console displays a per-route 1h heatmap of kernel cost and a drilldown to sampled traces sufficient to reproduce a 95th percentile tail event
End-to-end latency overhead of instrumentation < 2% p50 and < 8% p99 under typical load when sampling at default rate (1%)
tasks: Design: define lifecycle_id format and TTL; propose NVTX naming convention and label set
Prototype: implement adaptive sampler in the scheduler that uses exponential backoff under sustained high qps
Instrument: tag NVTX ranges on kernel launch/complete and attach kernel_fingerprint computed from kernel selector
Exporter: add OTLP label mapping and a rollup that emits per-kernel counters at 1s/60s buckets
Console: wire sampled traces into existing heatmap UI and add toggle to view sampled vs aggregate metrics
Testing: run chaos/soak with variant sampling rates and measure instrumentation overhead and signal fidelity
design_decisions: Sampling: use hybrid policy — default 1% probabilistic + adaptive rate-limit (max sampled/sec per host) to avoid burst pollution
Lifecycle ID: 10-char base62 with monotonic host prefix; stored in per-request context and propagated into trace/span attributes
NVTX naming: runtime.kernel.<phase>.<kernel_shortname> (e.g., runtime.kernel.prefill.flash_attn) to keep span searchable in traces
Kernel fingerprint: 8-hex of sha1(kernel_selector_config) to allow grouping without exposing full config
Exporter mapping: sampled spans include lifecycle_id; non-sampled flows still emit aggregated counters tagged by attention_path and kernel_fingerprint
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: instrumentation overhead spikes under high sampling — mitigate with adaptive rate-limiter and sampling budget per host
Risk: lifecycle_id proliferation causing cardinality blowup in metrics — mitigate with short TTL and only include lifecycle_id on sampled traces and short retention for that label in metrics storage
Risk: mismatch between kernel fingerprint and human-readable kernel variants — provide a lookup table service that maps fingerprint -> human-readable name for Console UI
